document.section_title: Greet the staff with こんにちは

blocks.headline: The greeting in kana and romaji
blocks.short: こんにちは (konnichiwa) is the daytime greeting; the final は is pronounced wa here.
blocks.deep: こんにちは (konnichiwa) is the standard daytime greeting in Japanese. It is written こ・ん・に・ち・は; in this fixed greeting the final は is pronounced wa. Say it evenly: ko-n-ni-chi-wa.

blocks.headline: When to say it
blocks.short: Use it on entering or meeting someone in the daytime: it opens the interaction.
blocks.deep: Say it when you enter a shop or meet someone during the day. It opens the interaction; it is neither a request nor a farewell.

blocks.headline: Say it back
blocks.short: Play the reference, then repeat こんにちは three times at the same rhythm.
blocks.deep: Play the pronunciation reference and repeat こんにちは three times, matching the rhythm ko-n-ni-chi-wa. The recording is the model; your own saying is the practice, and this page does not assess pronunciation.

blocks.headline: A staff member looks up as you enter the shop. What do you say?
blocks.short: Enter, then say konnichiwa once, clearly.
blocks.deep:
Choose the daytime greeting rather than a request or a farewell
Form the five sounds ko-n-ni-chi-wa
Say it once, clearly, as you enter
Answer: こんにちは (konnichiwa)

blocks.headline: Recap
blocks.short: こんにちは is the daytime greeting; は sounds as wa here.
blocks.deep: こんにちは (konnichiwa) is the standard daytime greeting. The final は in this fixed greeting is pronounced wa. Romaji is a scaffold while you learn the sounds, not a second answer.
